# Higher-order generic inference

The P0-G contract freezes 48 authored forms across eight ES5/ES2022,
CommonJS/ESNext and strictFunctionTypes profiles. Strict null checks remain on,
with explicit ES5 libraries. All 24 original discovery source strings and their
module files are unchanged; their original emitDeclarationOnly discovery profile
is replayed separately. Primary profiles emit JavaScript for syntax/execution.

Native TypeScript 5.9.3 calibration and independent replay agree on 384 complete
observations: 352 accepts /32 rejects, 424 exact declaration files, 704 isolated
positive/negative consumers, 424 selected-edition parses and 48 executions.
Six executable forms include real implementations; imported execution loads
the actual emitted module graph in both CommonJS and ESNext. A separate four-test
guard requires deliberate imported-runtime failures to be rejected.

The original discovery includes 20 differences and four agreements. The expanded
accepted-P0-F baseline has 336 complete differences /48 agreements: 116 incorrect
rejections, 204 declaration differences and 16 diagnostic differences. A test-first
Rust public-boundary run reproduces every one of the 384 baseline observations
before production changes. These baseline results are failures, not acceptance.

FROZEN.json binds the input/reference and twelve separate boundary controls to
the pinned compiler implementation and actual libraries. Resource/parser limits,
ambient owners and runtime-authority refusals have zero direct-agreement credit.
New inferred parameters must retain owner identities and bounded work.

Declaration inventories and diagnostics compare without normalization. Build-only
manifests are retained separately. The four original agreement controls and every
original difference remain mandatory. Native reference adapters are verification
only; never regenerate expected output from BlueTSC behavior.

The implementation must also pass the complete source-bound Native/local/Windows,
map/project/tooling gates before P0-G is checked or committed. Broader feature
rows remain open and full TypeScript parity remains OFF. See the phase directory's
HIGHER_ORDER_INFERENCE_FOLLOWUP.md for the complete acceptance contract.
